sections.title: Look Back (Review)
paragraphs: Pray for one another.
Read
Adam and Eve had children, and their children had children, and their children had children, until the whole world was filled with people.

sections.title: Look Up (New Teaching)
paragraphs: Read

Some years later, God spoke to a man named Abraham. He said, “Leave your home, your country, your relatives, and go to the land that I will show you. I will make a huge nation of people from your descendants. I will bless you and make you famous, and you will be a blessing to others. All the families on earth will be blessed through you.” So Abraham left as God had instructed and he worshipped God.

sections.title: When Abraham was old, God promised to give him a son. God told him, “Look up into the sky and count the stars if you can. That’s how many descendants you will have!” Abraham believed God, and because he believed God, God considered him to be in right relationship with Him
paragraphs: God kept His promise to Abraham and gave him a son. And his son had sons and their sons had sons until Abraham’s descendants were very numerous. These people became known as the Israelites (the children of Israel). They were also called the Hebrews, and this story is according to the word of God.
Read
Let’s read some verses from the Holy Scriptures, the Bible, that relate to this story.
Genesis 12:1–9
Read

These verses teach us that God, by His grace, calls ordinary and unworthy people for His good purpose. He called Abraham and promised to bless him and his family. And God's promise did not stop with Abraham — He promised that the people of the whole world would be blessed through him! This blessing finds its full meaning in Jesus Christ, who is Abraham's descendant, and through whom God's love is offered to every person.
Ask
What did you learn from these Scriptures?
Think a little — how will you practice what you have learned?

sections.title: Look Forward (Obedience)
paragraphs: Do
Abraham and his wife were nearly 100 years old when their son was born! If you ever feel hopeless, remember that it is never too late for God to keep his promise.
Ask
I hope you enjoyed this story. When can we meet again?
Do you think someone else should hear this story?
